newsitem.title: UK: Med dirty tanker rates still firm, may have peaked.
newsitem.headline: Med dirty tanker rates still firm, may have peaked.

text.p: The Mediterranean continued to outshine the rest of the world crude tanker market on Friday, but brokers said the recent rise in rates for 80,000 tonne vessels showed signs of peaking.
Rates for 80,000 tonne vessels were heard to have hit as high as W175 by the end of the week as tonnage in the area remained tight, although some thought this situation was set to slacken.
"The market has now reached a peak of W175 but it is unlikely to stay here long," shipbrokers Galbraith's said in their weekly report.
The Middle East market remained steady to slightly weaker with rates for very large crude carriers headed for Japan quoted at W65 against W67.5 seen on Thursday.

Galbraith's predicted little change in rates out of the are over the coming week. "Most major players appear to have booked the majority of their first half liftings and there are enough ships left in that period for the odd charterer who hasn't or, indeed, for the ship that is running late," they said.
Rates out of West Africa were little changed with 130,000 tonners commanding around W95 while 250,000 tonners were seen fixed at around W62.5.
"The volumes in this are can probably be described as 'fairly average', with supply/demand also pretty much in balance," said Galbraith's.

The Caribbean upcoast market was also unchanged with 70,000 tonne vessels commanding roughly W167.5. Brokers said rates in the area may improve after reports that some crude vessels were headed out of the region for the Mediterranean.
The UK/cont market was little changed with rates for 80,000 tonnes quoted at around W115-120.
